skill.name: engineering-loop
skill.description: Drive an authorized repository change through a verified local loop: baseline, reproduce, implement, test, review, and report evidence. Use for end-to-end features or fixes that should continue autonomously until observable acceptance criteria pass; do not use for explanation-only, review-only, or production operations.
skill.summary: Complete repository changes through a disciplined local development, testing, review, and evidence cycle.
skill.author: phelan164

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by prose and inline Markdown formatting. The skill defines a bounded local engineering workflow without executable shell logic, prompt injection, or data-exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: - Did any fix change a public contract, migration requirement, or operational

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited line asks whether a fix changed a public contract, migration requirement, or operational assumption. It does not instruct system reconnaissance or unauthorized discovery.
The backticks are Markdown formatting around the filename AGENTS.md. The line only instructs the agent to read repository guidance and contains no executable shell or Ruby command.

content.user_title: Complete Repository Changes with Verified Evidence
content.value_statement: Repository changes can fail when implementation, testing, and review are disconnected. This skill manages a complete local engineering loop with explicit evidence and stop conditions.
actual_capabilities: Establishes repository guidance, acceptance criteria, working tree state, and baseline validation before implementation.
Reproduces defects or records current feature behavior before selecting a bounded change.
Runs focused checks before repository-required broader validation.
Classifies product, test, environment, assumption, and external blocker failures.
Reviews the complete diff and reverifies consequential corrections.
Reports changed behavior, validation outcomes, unresolved findings, risks, and blockers.
limitations: It does not perform production operations without explicit user authorization.
It cannot proceed when required secrets, permissions, infrastructure, or product decisions are unavailable.
It does not replace project-specific repository guidance or validation commands.
It is not intended for explanation-only or review-only requests.

use_cases.title: Implement a Focused Feature
use_cases.description: Complete a repository feature from baseline inspection through tests, diff review, and final evidence.

use_cases.title: Resolve a Reproducible Defect
use_cases.description: Reproduce a defect, add regression coverage, implement a bounded fix, and verify affected behavior.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Cross-Stack Change
use_cases.description: Track acceptance criteria, validation levels, contract effects, and blockers across several repository layers.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Small Defect
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the engineering loop to reproduce and fix [defect]. Preserve unrelated changes, run focused tests, review the diff, and report evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a clear defect and known repository.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [feature] with these acceptance criteria: [criteria]. Establish the baseline, add appropriate tests, run required checks, and summarize residual risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs an end-to-end feature implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate an Intermittent Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [failure] using a bounded reproducer and ranked hypotheses. Isolate the cause, add regression coverage, implement the smallest fix, and reverify.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced engineer faces a timing-sensitive or intermittent defect.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a High-Risk Cross-Stack Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete [change] across [layers]. Track contracts, migrations, authorization boundaries, data integrity, validation levels, review findings, and explicit stop conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead needs rigorous coordination and evidence across repository boundaries.

output_examples.input: Fix the duplicate invoice submission defect and add regression coverage.
output: Fixed duplicate submission handling in the owning request path.
Added a regression test covering repeated invoice requests.
Focused tests and the required broader checks passed.
Reviewed the final diff; no unresolved consequential findings remain.

output_examples.input: Add account export with authorization checks and report any blockers.
output: Implemented authorized account export with explicit ownership validation.
Added success, forbidden, and malformed-request coverage.
Focused validation passed, but the full integration suite requires unavailable infrastructure.
The remaining blocker and exact required service were documented.

output_examples.input: Investigate an intermittent cache invalidation failure.
output: Created a bounded reproducer and recorded the distinguishing failure signature.
Tested ranked timing and key-normalization hypotheses independently.
Isolated the cause, added regression coverage, and removed temporary instrumentation.
The original reproduction and affected repository checks passed.

best_practices: Define observable acceptance criteria and a safe baseline before changing code.
Run the narrowest relevant check after each bounded change, then complete required broader validation.
Preserve unrelated work and report unrun checks, residual risks, and blockers explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not weaken assertions, remove coverage, or hide errors to make validation pass.
Do not repeat identical failing commands without classifying the failure and revisiting assumptions.
Do not deploy, migrate, merge, publish, or query production without explicit authorization.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for authorized repository features or fixes that require implementation, testing, review, and evidence.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing dirty working tree?
faq.answer: Yes. It inspects the working tree and preserves unrelated user-owned changes.

faq.question: Does it always add a regression test first?
faq.answer: It adds a failing regression test first when practical and uses other observable evidence when that approach is unsuitable.

faq.question: How does it handle repeated failures?
faq.answer: After two identical failures, it stops blind retries and rechecks the environment, target, permissions, and assumptions.

faq.question: Can it deploy or modify production?
faq.answer: No. Production queries, deployments, migrations, merges, and publishing require explicit user authorization.

faq.question: What does the final report include?
faq.answer: It includes changed behavior, important decisions, validation outcomes, review findings, unrun checks, residual risks, and blockers.
